properties.name: writeSteps
properties.hint: Desktop steps only. Leave empty when no step saves, posts or submits.
properties.description: Desktop steps only: the numbers of the steps that save, post or submit, as the approver declared them (the change list numbers every step; the safety flags list the candidates). Listed steps are signed as writes, so the desktop runner lets them act on the write controls and gated keys of its policy. The runner refuses a write only on those: leaving a step unlisted does not stop it from saving unless its control is in the runner policy. Map it from the approval answer. Browser steps refuse a value here.

properties.name: checkOnly
properties.description: Whether to only report what this node signs for: the name of its RPA Site Login, and whether the signature of an approved version on the input item (an active row of the steps table) verifies with this node's RPA Step Signing key and Site Login. RPA: 5 Import a bot does this before its review page.

properties.displayName: Imported steps make no form submissions or writes; Requests That Only Read still pass. Each step list runs once and is replayed in a fresh browser, so allow about twice Options → Max Seconds per step list. On sites with an authenticator code, the import needs either the TOTP Secret in the Site Login or Options → One-Time Code Workflow, and Max Seconds must leave room for up to a 30 s wait. What passes comes out on Repaired Steps for approval and Sign Steps. Desktop steps (from a UiPath project, a step document or an RPA recording) are not replayed: they go to approval as written.

options.name: allowedHosts
options.description: Extra sites the browser may open or load files from, separated by commas. Exact hosts only, no wildcards. Leave empty when a Site Login is attached: the credential sets the allowed sites.

options.name: allowPrivateNetwork
options.description: Whether the allowed sites may be on a private network address, such as 10.x, 192.168.x or localhost. Must be set directly, not with an expression.

options.name: idPattern
options.description: Optional. A regular expression that matches the ID every record has, such as INV-\d{4} for INV-0417. When set, the node keeps only rows whose ID matches, and removes duplicates by ID. To check the count against a total the page states, set Stated Total Pattern. Leave empty to return everything found. Required for AI repair.
options.hint: Not sure? Paste one real ID into regex101.com and describe its shape: digits \d, letters [A-Z], repeats {4}.

options.name: totalPattern
options.description: A regular expression whose first group is the total the page states, such as (\d+) results. The row count must equal it; confirmed is true only then.

options.name: requiredFields
options.description: Comma-separated row fields that must not be empty. A row missing one fails the run.

options.name: emptyPattern
options.description: Lets a run with no rows succeed, but only when the page shows text matching this (case-insensitive). Leave empty to treat zero rows as a failure.

options.name: variables
options.description: Values for {{var.name}} in the steps. In Run Steps, a password or another secret goes in an RPA Secret Variables credential instead: a value here is masked only where a secret fill or a desktop step types it.
options.hint: Not n8n expressions; {{var.name}} is replaced inside steps.

options.name: name
options.description: Names the step list. Required for a first run (empty steps with AI Repair on). With signed steps, it must equal the signed name.

options.name: expectedVersion
options.description: With signed steps, the signed version must equal this whole number. Map it from the newest active row, so an edited version column fails.

options.name: allowUnsignedWrites
options.description: Whether unsigned steps may sign in, submit a form or download through a form. With this on, whoever can set the steps drives the Site Login and, on a login page that copies typed values into the page, can read its password out through step outcomes. Turn it on only when everyone who can set the steps is trusted with that credential. Must be set directly, not with an expression.

options.name: deliverUnconfirmed
options.description: Whether rows read during AI repair go to Data even when the proof in a fresh browser did not pass. Must be set directly, not with an expression.

options.name: maxActions
options.description: Most browser actions the chat model may take while repairing

options.name: maxTokens
options.description: Most chat model tokens one run may use

options.name: codeWorkflowId
options.description: The workflow that returns the sign-in's one-time code when the sign-in takes it from a workflow ("source": "workflow"). It starts with an Execute Workflow Trigger, gets requestedAt and returns one item whose code field holds 6 to 10 digits; publish it first. In Import Steps, a recorded sign-in then takes its code from it (a step document sets "source" itself); give Run Steps the same workflow. Must be set directly, not with an expression.

options.name: codeTimeout
options.description: How long the sign-in waits for the One-Time Code Workflow. Max Seconds still bounds the whole run.

options.name: version
options.description: The version the imported steps get. 1 for a new bot. To change an approved bot, give one more than the highest version any row of its name has in the steps table (active, rejected or superseded), so the new steps are a new version under the same name and no two rows share a name and version: the import form does this. A version in a step document is never used.

options.name: approvedBeforeHandOver
options.description: Whether this workflow approves the imported steps before it hands the workflow file over, as the import form does. When on, the notes in the workflow file do not ask to import and approve the steps.

options.name: importFormName
options.description: The name of the workflow whose form imports and approves these steps. The notes in the workflow file send the reader there to change the steps or sign them again. Empty: RPA: 5 Import a bot. The import form sets it.

options.name: importFormAddress
options.description: The address of that form (http or https), shown beside its name in the workflow file's notes. Empty: no address. The import form sets it.

options.name: breakerResetKey
options.description: With a Site Login, a failed login stops further logins until its username, password or TOTP Secret is changed, which gets one try. If the login was right, or the account is unlocked now, change this value (for example to today's date) to allow the next login. Type it, not an expression: a login that fails stays blocked for the rest of the execution.

options.name: saveTrace
options.description: When to attach a scrubbed browser trace as binary "trace"

options.name: maxItems
options.description: More input items than this fail the execution before any run
